breakfast.name: Draniki (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate potatoes and onion, squeeze out liquid
Mix with eggs, flour, salt, pepper
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until golden on both sides
Serve with sour cream
breakfast.description: Crispy potato pancakes — the most iconic Belarusian dish.

breakfast.name: Syrniki (Curd Cheese Fritters)
instructions: Mix cheese, eggs, sugar, flour, vanilla
Shape into thick patties
Fry in butter on medium heat until golden
Serve with sour cream and jam

imageCredit.author: Tatyana Morozyuk, color processing by Off-shell

breakfast.name: Bliny (Thin Pancakes)
ingredients: Sour cream and jam to serve
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, sugar, salt
Add flour gradually, whisk until smooth and thin as cream
Add melted butter
Heat buttered pan, pour thin layer of batter
Cook until edges lift and bottom is golden, flip
Stack on plate, serve with sour cream, jam, or savory fillings
breakfast.description: Paper-thin pancakes stacked high — filled with sour cream, mushrooms, or jam. Maslenitsa (Butter Week) means bliny every day.

lunch.name: Borscht (Belarusian Style)
instructions: Simmer meat in water 30 min
Add beets and vinegar, cook 10 min
Add potatoes, carrots, onion
Add cabbage and tomato paste
Simmer until vegetables tender
Serve with sour cream and dill
lunch.description: Belarusian beet soup, heartier than its Ukrainian cousin.

lunch.name: Kalduny (Stuffed Dumplings)
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, 1 egg, water, salt
Filling: 300g ground pork, 1 onion, salt, pepper
instructions: Make dough, rest 20 min
Mix pork with onion and seasoning
Roll dough thin, cut circles
Fill, fold and pinch edges
Boil in salted water until they float
Serve with sour cream and dill
lunch.description: Belarusian meat dumplings, a close cousin of pelmeni.

lunch.name: Vereshchaka (Sausage in Beet Sauce)
ingredients: 500ml beet kvass (or beet juice with vinegar)
instructions: Slice sausage into thick rounds
Brown in pan
Sauté onion, add flour, cook 2 min
Add beet kvass, bay leaf
Simmer 20 min until sauce thickens and turns deep ruby
Serve with draniki or boiled potatoes
lunch.description: An old Belarusian sauce dish — sausage in ruby-red beet kvass sauce. Named after a 19th-century Minsk cook.

lunch.name: Draniki (Crispy Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate potatoes on fine grater — squeeze out excess liquid but save the starch
Grate onion into potatoes
Add egg, flour, salt, pepper, and the reserved potato starch
Mix well — batter should be thick
Fry spoonfuls in hot oil/lard until deeply golden and crispy on both sides
Drain briefly
Serve immediately with cold sour cream and dill
These must be eaten hot — they lose their crunch within minutes
lunch.description: Belarus's national dish — crispy lacy potato pancakes fried in lard and served with cold sour cream. The ASMR crunch videos and the passionate debates about proper grating technique (fine only!) have made draniki a viral Eastern European food star.

dinner.name: Machanka (Pork in Sour Cream Sauce)
instructions: Brown pork ribs and sliced sausage
Sauté onion in butter, add flour
Stir in sour cream, add water to thin
Add meats back, simmer 20 min
Serve over thick potato pancakes
dinner.description: Rich pork and sausage smothered in sour cream gravy.

dinner.name: Babka (Potato Casserole)
instructions: Fry bacon and onions until golden
Grate potatoes, squeeze out liquid
Mix with bacon, onions, eggs, sour cream, season
Pour into greased baking dish
Bake at 180°C 60 min until crusty on top
dinner.description: A golden, crusty potato casserole studded with bacon.

dinner.name: Kletski (Potato Dumplings)
ingredients: 6 potatoes (half grated raw, half boiled and mashed)
instructions: Squeeze liquid from grated raw potato, save the starch that settles
Mix raw and mashed potato with egg, starch, salt
Shape into small balls or ovals — can stuff with meat if desired
Drop into salted boiling water
Cook until they float, then 3 more min
Serve with sour cream and shkvarki scattered over
dinner.description: Belarusian potato dumplings — the combination of raw and cooked potato gives them a unique dense, chewy texture.

snacks.name: Kolduny s Gribami (Mushroom Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: 300g mushrooms, 1 onion, butter, dill, salt, pepper
instructions: Make dough, rest
Sauté mushrooms and onion in butter
Roll dough thin, cut circles, fill
Boil until they float
Serve with melted butter and dill

snacks.name: Tsibriki (Fried Potato Balls)
instructions: Squeeze excess liquid from grated potato
Mix with egg, flour, salt
Shape into small balls or thick discs
Fry in oil until golden all over
Serve hot with sour cream
snacks.description: Fried potato balls — draniki's round cousin. Quick, crispy, always served with sour cream.

desserts.name: Zefir (Marshmallow Confection)
instructions: Cook apple purée until thick
Dissolve agar in water, boil to make syrup with sugar
Whip egg white, gradually add apple purée
Stream in hot syrup while whipping
Pipe into rosettes on parchment
Let set 24 hours, dust with powdered sugar
desserts.description: Soft, airy marshmallow confections made with apple.

desserts.name: Kulaga (Berry Pudding)
instructions: Cook berries with a little water until soft
Mix rye flour with cold water, add to berries
Stir until thickened
Sweeten with honey
Serve warm or cold with bread
desserts.description: Ancient Belarusian berry pudding thickened with rye flour — a taste of the Slavic forests. Best with freshly picked wild berries.

drinks.name: Kompot (Fruit Compote Drink)
instructions: Bring water and sugar to boil
Add fruit, simmer 10 min
Cool to room temperature
Strain or serve with fruit
Chill and serve
drinks.description: A light, fruity beverage served cold.

drinks.name: Krupnik (Honey Spiced Vodka)
instructions: Simmer water with honey and spices 10 min
Strain out spices
Cool slightly, add vodka
Bottle and let flavors meld 1 week
drinks.description: Traditional honey-spiced vodka served warm or cold.

drinks.name: Beet Kvass (Burachniy Kvas)
instructions: Place beet cubes in a jar with water
Add sugar, salt, rye bread
Cover with cloth, ferment at room temperature 3-5 days
Strain — the liquid should be deep ruby and slightly fizzy
Serve cold or use as a base for cold beet soup
drinks.description: Fermented beet drink — tangy, earthy, ruby-red. Used both as a drink and a cooking ingredient in traditional Belarusian borscht.
